Keysight Technologies Inc reported revenue of $1.85 billion for the third fiscal quarter ended 2026-07-31, growth of 36.54 per cent from a year earlier, with net income of $397 million, growth of 107.85 per cent [D1]. Income from operations was $461 million against $234 million a year earlier, growth of 97.01 per cent [D1]. Communications Solutions Group revenue was $1.35 billion, up 43.09 per cent, and Electronic Industrial Solutions Group revenue was $501 million, up 21.6 per cent [D1].

Fourth fiscal quarter revenue guidance is $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion with earnings per share of $3.34 to $3.40 on a weighted diluted share count of approximately 172 million shares [D1]. The midpoint of the revenue range represents year over year growth of approximately 37 per cent [D1]. Management said the quarter exceeded the high end of its guidance range for both revenue and earnings per share and raised its fourth quarter and full year outlook [D3].

Demand for testing solutions linked to artificial intelligence infrastructure was a major contributor to the quarter, and wireline revenue surpassed the wireless business for the first time in the company's history [D2]. Management said demand is far exceeding its ability to supply and that the pipeline continues to grow strongly [D3]. Management expects the 6G opportunity to be larger than the 5G opportunity, with customers moving into funded development programs [D4]. Management expects fourth quarter orders to be slightly up from the third quarter and described the funnel as being at an all time high [D4].

Analysts pressed management on the sustainability of demand and on whether supply constraints are limiting near term guidance [D3]. Management said the supply chain will remain the governor of near term revenue and that the supply situation is likely to be nonlinear [D3]. Management cautioned that one time tariff impacts pulled up fiscal 2026 profitability and will not repeat [D3]. Management said the supply environment is less flexible today than a year earlier and that it is planning over a longer horizon for supply [D3]. Coverage questions whether the artificial intelligence growth leaves room for error on valuation and whether further stock price gains are supported by fundamentals [D3]. Analyst price targets sit substantially above the current trading level [D2]. The stock trades at a forward price to earnings multiple of 20.66 against a trailing multiple of 45.89 on trailing earnings per share of 7.38 [D5].
